<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par144 />{{GHGmargin-letter|144|d}}
'''3.''' The indefinite personal subject (our ''they, one'', the French ''on'', and the German ''man''<ref>In {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=9|verse=9}} {{GHGheb|text=הָאִישׁ}} (prop. ''the man'') is used in exactly the same sense as our ''one''.</ref>) is expressed—

(''a'') By the 3rd person singular masculine, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=קָרָא|translate=one}} (sc. any ''one who named'' it, see the Rem.) ''called'' (or ''calls'') it, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=11|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=16|verse=14|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=19|verse=22|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=15|verse=23}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּקְרָא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=35|verse=8}}, 10, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=2|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=9|verse=5}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַיֹּא֫מֶר|translate=one said}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=48|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=16|verse=4}};<ref>Elsewhere in such cases {{GHGheb|text=וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ}} usually occurs (but not in the perfect, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=23|verse=22}}), so that it is doubtful whether the present reading of {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=48|verse=1}}, &c., would not be better explained according to {{GHGpar|7|d}}, note. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=48|verse=2}} for the extraordinary {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּגֵּד}} the common form {{GHGheb|text=וַיֻּגַּד}} is to be read; so in 50:26 for {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּישֶׂם}} (after a plural) either {{GHGheb|text=וַיּוּשַׂם}} or the 3rd plur.; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=21|verse=26}} {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּקְבְּרוּ}}.</ref> other examples are {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=38|verse=28}} ''one put out a hand''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=23|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=22|verse=38}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=6|verse=10}} {{GHGheb|text=וְרָפָא לוֹ|translate=and one heals them}}; 8:4 ({{GHGheb|text=יִשָּׂא}}); 46:7 ({{GHGheb|text=יִצְעַק}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=6|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=2|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=27|verse=23}}; by the 3rd singular feminine ({{GHGheb|text=יָֽלְדָה}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=26|verse=59}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|144|e}}
Rem. The Jewish commentators, following the Arab grammarians, usually explain these singulars by the addition of the participle (generally determinate) of the same stem, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=קָרָא הַקֹּרֵא}}. This view is supported by the fact that such a complement sometimes occurs, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=16|verse=10}} {{GHGheb|text=יִדְרֹךְ הַדֹּרֵךְ|translate=the treader treads out}}, for ''one treads out''; 28:4, 24 (''doth one plow continually?''); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=17|verse=6}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=18|verse=32}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=22|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=17|verse=9}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=33|verse=4}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=9|verse=23}}; with an indeterminate participle (as in Arabic, e.g. ''qāla qāʾilun'', ''a sayer says'', i.e. ''some one says''), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=6|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=9|verse=1}}; cf. above, {{GHGpar|116|t}}, and, on the whole question, Driver on {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=16|verse=4}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|144|f}}
(''b'') Very frequently by the 3rd plural masculine, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=29|verse=2}} ''for out of that well'' {{GHGheb|text=יַשְׁקוּ|translate=they}} (i.e. people generally) ''watered the flocks''; 26:18, 35:5, 41:14, 49:31, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=1|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=38|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=12|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=18|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=34|verse=20|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=2|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=2|verse=7}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|144|g}}
Rem. The 3rd plur. also is sometimes used to express an indefinite subject, where the context does not admit of a human agent or at least not of several, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=34|verse=27}}. In such a case the 3rd plur. comes to be equivalent to a passive, as very commonly in Aramaic (see Kautzsch’s {{GHGcite|title=Gramm. des Bibl. Aram.}}, § 96. 1 ''c''); e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=7|verse=3}} ''wearisome nights'' {{GHGheb|text=מִנּוּ־לִי|translate=have they allotted to me}} (equivalent to ''were allotted to me''; to make ‘invisible powers’ the subject is a merely artificial device); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=4|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=6|verse=2|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=18|verse=18|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=19|verse=26|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=34|verse=20|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=32|verse=25}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=63|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=2|verse=22}} (in parallelism with a passive); 9:11.

{{GHGmargin-letter|144|h}}
(''c'') By the 2nd singular masculine, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=7|verse=25}} {{GHGheb|text=לֹֽא־תָבוֹא שָׁ֫מָּה|translate=one will}} (or ''can'') ''not come thither'' (prop. ''thou wilt''...); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=23|verse=37}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=19|verse=25}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=30|verse=28|hidebook=1}} (unless the reading should be {{GHGheb|text=תִּתָּפֵשׂ}}). Cf. also {{GHGheb|text=עַד־בֹּֽאֲךָ}} or simply {{GHGheb|text=בֹּֽאֲךָ}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=10|verse=19}}, 30, 13:10 {{GHGheb|text=בֹּֽאֲבָה}}) prop. ''until thy coming'', i.e. ''until one comes''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|144|i}}
(''d'') By the plural of the participle, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=38|verse=23}} ''and all thy wives and thy children'' {{GHGheb|text=מֽוֹצִאִים}} (prop. ''are they bringing out''=) ''they will bring out'', &c.; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=32|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=13|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=6|verse=10}} (''for some are coming to slay thee'')<section end=par144 /><noinclude>
